methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a correct model, explain it in plain language, repair any gap, then explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining forces you to connect the membrane idea to water movement and exposes missing links.
how: Answer from memory in your own words.
Use the feedback to fix one specific gap.
Explain again more clearly and more completely.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state both ideas accurately and repair the main gap in your first attempt.
personalization: Use the current task as the baseline.
Keep the explanation short and concrete.
Focus on the relationship between membrane selectivity and water movement.

activities.label: Model the membrane idea
activities.title: Selective barrier of cell membrane
activities.body: Read the model and note the main rule. Then be ready to explain it from memory.

essentialIdeas: Cell membrane as a selective barrier lets some substances cross more easily than others.

activities.label: Explain the membrane
activities.title: Explain the membrane rule
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain what the membrane does. Then compare your answer with the model.
activities.concept: Cell membrane as a selective barrier
activities.correctAnswer: The cell membrane is a selective barrier that lets some substances cross more easily than others.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names selective permeability and the idea that passage differs by substance. A common gap is saying the membrane blocks everything or lets everything through.

activities.label: Repair the osmosis idea
activities.title: Fix the water movement idea
activities.body: Correct the gap in one short response. Focus on what moves and in which direction.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The misconception is that osmosis is the movement of solute through the membrane, rather than the movement of water.
activities.correctAnswer: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: This answer must name water, not solute, and show the direction from higher to lower water concentration. The key repair is separating water movement from solute movement.

activities.label: Reexplain osmosis
activities.title: Explain osmosis again
activities.body: Explain osmosis again in your own words. Keep it short and specific.
activities.correctAnswer: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: A strong answer keeps water as the moving substance and includes the membrane and concentration direction. If you mention solute instead of water, revisit the repair step.

activities.label: Check recognition
activities.title: Which statement matches osmosis?
activities.body: Choose the best statement. Then check your reasoning.
choices: Water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
Sugar moves across a membrane from lower water concentration to higher water concentration.
Water moves only when the membrane has no gaps at all.
Osmosis means every substance crosses the membrane at the same rate.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: Correct. Osmosis is about the net movement of water, and the membrane helps make that movement selective.

items.essentialIdea: Cell membrane selectively permits some substances to cross more easily than others.

check.title: Membrane passage
check.prompt: How does a cell membrane control what crosses it?
check.referenceAnswer: It is selectively permeable, so some substances cross more easily than others.
check.feedback: The key idea is unequal passage, not complete openness or blockage.

items.essentialIdea: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

check.title: Water movement in osmosis
check.prompt: What is osmosis in terms of water and membranes?
check.referenceAnswer: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.
check.feedback: Osmosis specifically involves water moving across a selective membrane.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify osmosis
choices: Net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane
Movement of solute particles across a cell membrane
Movement of water from lower to higher water concentration
Any movement of substances through a membrane
